svg.aria-label: How to write અને: 3 parts, અ, ન, ે, one after another
svg.title: Writing અને
svg.desc: 3 parts written one after another: અ, ન, ે (gujarati). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which in Gujarati is the order they are typed: each sign comes after its consonant, even the i sign, which sits to the left of it. Each sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: અ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, અ animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ન: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ન animation, first and second SVG paths <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ે: Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/6_ke.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the e sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>. Source notes on variation: અ: The teaching app animates અ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper-left tip, sweeps clockwise around the open left curve, continues through the broad lower body, rises into the middle shoulder, and finishes through the small right arch. The animation then lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate right stem before curving into the lower-right foot. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph has the same open left curve, joined lower body, middle shoulder, small right arch, and separate full-height right stem, but its printed proportions are broader and its joins more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's body-before-right-stem order and one-lift evidence while fitting those movements to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, or slant either run differently. ન: The teaching app animates ન as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper left of the small loop, circles clockwise around that loop, then continues right across the long shoulder to the right-spine junction. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate tall right spine before turning through the lower-right foot. The remaining path slots are empty. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the small left loop, long shoulder, tall right spine, and lower foot, but its printed loop is wider and its shoulder and spine straighter than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's loop-and-shoulder-before-right-spine order and one-lift evidence while fitting both runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the loop, shoulder, spine, foot, and terminals differently. ે: In the template for કે, and in all 33 consonant rows whose consonant keeps its bare outline, ે is one pen-down run that starts at the upper-left tip, arcs right and comes down to the lower right, where it meets the consonant. t30apps, already cited for એ, sweeps the matching high arc from left to right, last. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: 162 of its 165 stored prototypes of the e sign (98%) are one stroke, most running from the upper left down to the lower right. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer.
svg.text: How it is written — 3 parts, one after another
Part 1 of 3 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 4 movements
Part 3 of 3 — one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
Part 1: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, અ animation, first and second SVG paths
Part 2: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ન animation, first and second SVG paths
Part 3: stroke order after Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/6_ke.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0):
the e sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
